name: navigator.oscpu, vendor, productSub
plain: Legacy engine strings: oscpu (Firefox), vendor, vendorSub, productSub, cpuClass.
meaning: Quick tells for the rendering engine and OS. vendor is Google Inc., Apple Computer, Inc. or empty (Firefox); productSub is 20030107 on Chromium and Safari, 20100101 on Firefox. Used to catch spoofed browsers.

access.persistence: read fresh on every page load; nothing stored
access.iframe: Readable from cross-origin iframes too (same values)

fields.name: vendor
fields.range: Google Inc., Apple Computer, Inc., empty

fields.name: oscpu
fields.range: Firefox only, e.g. Intel Mac OS X 10.15

limits.headline: Can see old engine labels that tell Chrome, Safari, and Firefox apart
limits.user_action: Nothing. It happens when the page loads
can: Check vendor, productSub, and oscpu text
Tell the browser engine and OS family
Catch a browser that is faking its identity
cannot: See your exact device or OS version
See anything in oscpu on Chrome or Safari
See your name, location, or accounts
Tell you apart from others using the same browser
limits.differs: The oscpu value comes back only in Firefox. Other browsers return nothing.

story.what_it_is: Old engine strings like oscpu, vendor and productSub that quickly show which browser engine you run.
story.for_you: You never see them. A site can read one short string and know you use Firefox, Chrome or Safari, even if you changed the user agent.
story.for_makers: Different engines return different values, so these are quick tells. Fraud teams use them to catch fakes. Developers use them to work around engine differences.

use_cases.example: A bot defence service sees vendor says Google Inc. but oscpu exists, which only Firefox has, and flags the visitor.
An ad verification script separates real browsers from headless tools by checking these fields.
A support page prints these values to help staff work out which engine a customer runs.
A browser game portal enables a fix for a known engine bug when it recognises the engine.
A traffic report separates Firefox, Safari and Chrome even when the user agent is hidden.
A bank adds a point to a login risk score when the engine tells disagree.

technical_bounds: Deprecated fields; values are constants per engine

linkedin.how: Collected as vendor, vendorSub, productSub, oscpu, cpuClass. Read by the LinkedIn APFC fingerprint script (48 features, alleged by BrowserGate, partly confirmed by BleepingComputer).
